targetText: The best tribute that we could give him is to commit ourselves to continuing with the same courage, the same sincerity, with the same skills the work he undertook with so much love and respect for Black people and Black civilizations.
explanation: Sankara rejects passive mourning for revolutionary thinkers like Cheikh Anta Diop, insisting that authentic tribute requires actively continuing their scientific and anti-colonial work. Diop dismantled colonial myths by documenting the African origins of civilization, establishing history as a battleground for liberation.

targetText: What have Black people done, what can or must they still do, to take responsibility for their own history and in that way contribute to Universal civilization [la civilisation de l'Universel]?
explanation: Sankara poses the foundational question of anti-colonial intellectual emancipation: oppressed peoples must seize responsibility for their own historical narrative rather than allowing imperialist powers to define their identity, worth, and future contributions to world civilization.

targetText: Because history has finally proved that Black people are right to organize and develop their active solidarity around already existing shared initiatives, both in Mother Africa and in the countries of the Diaspora. It is within this framework that the BI should be in the conscience of Black people geographically dispersed in a fragmented space, a reunifying symbol, the symbol of their shared will to preserve their cultural identities, their creative genius, and their dignity.
explanation: Connecting the anti-colonial struggles across continental Africa with civil rights and liberation movements in the diaspora, Sankara highlights shared historical origins and common resistance against slavery and imperialism as the foundation of enduring Pan-African solidarity.

targetText: This is why the Black Institute will not be confined, neither to itself, nor to its object, that is Black people. It will be open to other people. This is the essential condition for Black people to reassess their historical patrimony, to redefine their whole identity in the contemporary world. In our opinion, the Black Institute - its objectives - will always be to affirm itself and participate in cultural dialogue, which for us is the understanding between peoples regardless of their color.
explanation: Sankara warns against insular cultural nationalism, arguing that reclaiming African heritage is a dialectical step toward genuine universalism. True intercultural dialogue requires that historically oppressed nations participate as fully autonomous equals rather than colonized subjects.

targetText: Burkina Faso is only the humble initiator of a project, of a collective idea which is above all democratic, even universal, and therefore denationalized, depersonalized, in order to become the battle horse of all those who have always maintained, by whatever means, the hope of seeing the cultural unity of Black people through a framework of shared reflection. To this end, we should pay homage to the martyrs, to the political, artistic, scientific, literary struggles of all those who believed and believe in the dawn of "Universal Civilization," that is, in love and solidarity.
explanation: Demonstrating revolutionary humility and internationalism, Sankara presents Burkina Faso not as a dominant patron, but merely as a facilitator offering its resources to serve a shared democratic, Pan-African, and universal project of human liberation.
